events.what: Wang and Lu prove linear recoloring diameter for d-degenerate chordal graphs with t>=2d+1 colors and treewidth-k graphs with t>=2k+1 colors
Exact k-recoloring diameters of complete bipartite graphs K_{p,q}, k>=3
Exact maximum and minimum 3-coloring diameters over n-vertex trees

judgement.doubts: Wang–Lu could be read as a 'case' (graph class x colour range t>=2d+1 inside the conjecture's t>=d+2), which would make the status partial. I read it as a variant: it proves a stronger conclusion (linear) in a regime with far more colours than the conjecture's threshold, and the record gives no sign the quadratic bound at t>=2d+1 for these classes was open before; the paper's own framing (per the record) is a strengthening beyond the conjecture, not a new case of it. The other two papers refine exact constants for families already known to have linear diameter (trees d=1 proved pre-2024; K_{p,q}), which leaves the conjecture's question unchanged. Even under the rejected reading, 'progress' was wrong: a settled restriction is 'partial', not a bound.

corrections.why: F3/other: none of the three events moves a bound on the bullet's quadratic-diameter question at t>=d+2. The record itself says Wang–Lu works 'at a materially larger number of colors' and 'no case at the conjectured threshold t=d+2 was newly settled', which makes it a variant (stronger conclusion under different hypotheses); the tree and K_{p,q} papers sharpen constants for cases already known to be linear. Nothing survives step 1, and nothing resolved it before the snapshot, so the status is open.
F14: a 'progress' row cannot carry 'confirmed', and 'open' carries null.
other: nothing after the snapshot moves this bullet; the record's own what_would_settle_it notes that d=2 remains completely open.
